title: Palisade Docs — pricing while churn rises
decision_question: Should Palisade raise prices in 2027 while customer churn is rising, and if so, how?

initial_hypothesis.holder: CFO (with the CEO holding the opposite view)
initial_hypothesis.statement: Raise list prices 12% on every plan; churn is onboarding, not price ($10.3M).
initial_hypothesis.explanation: Both interpretations are partly right. The SMB churn rise is mostly a mix effect from the 2025 promotion cohort (≈4.9% monthly churn vs 2.1% for other SMB customers; mix effect ≈ 1.0 pp of the 1.1 pp rise) — supporting the CFO — but those customers leave over price when the discount ends and Inkwell has made SMB more price-competitive — supporting the CEO. A good answer differentiates by segment rather than adopting either view wholesale.

key_insights.text: Churn rise is concentrated in SMB (2.0% → 3.1%); mid-market rose modestly (0.6% → 0.8%), enterprise flat (0.2%). Revenue-weighted monthly churn rose from 0.83% to 1.19%.
Mix decomposition: non-promo SMB churn 2.0% → 2.1% (rate effect ≈ 0.1 pp); promotion cohort ≈ 4.9% implied; the promotion explains ≈ 1.0 pp of the 1.1 pp SMB increase.

Price is a real churn reason, but mainly for the promotion cohort at discount expiry (52% cite price) vs 18% for non-promo SMB; Inkwell's $9 plan and the win-rate fall (51% → 38%) make SMB price-sensitive.
The $10.3M is overstated: only renewing ARR reprices in 2027 and 60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7% → about $7.57M before any churn response (SMB $2.52M, mid-market $4.18M, enterprise $0.86M).
Mid-market and enterprise look price-inelastic (low churn, NRR 112%/118%, 2024 test showed no conversion effect, no Inkwell presence) — that is where an increase is safest and worth most.

A 12% increase is revenue-neutral if it causes about 10.7% extra loss of the repriced base. The 2023 SMB +8% increase lost about 3.6% extra customers and netted about 4.1% — but that was before Inkwell.
Activation (≥5 documents in month one) predicts retention; onboarding fixes for the promotion cohort are a separate lever from pricing.
The dashboard's 1.4% → 2.3% matches neither blended logo churn (1.71% → 2.62%) nor revenue-weighted churn (0.83% → 1.19%); a good answer works from the segment table and notes the undefined metric.

required_calculations.text: Segment churn comparison and/or revenue-weighted churn

required_calculations.tolerance: ±$0.5M; any correction for renewal timing or caps counts

decision_relevant_evidence.text: Segment churn table (SMB vs mid-market vs enterprise)
Promotion cohort size, activation and non-promo SMB churn 2.1%
Exit reasons by group (52% vs 18% citing price)
Inkwell $9 plan and SMB win-rate decline
Renewal timing and the 7% enterprise cap
2023 SMB price-increase history and 2024 mid-market test
Undefined dashboard churn metric vs the segment table

contradictory_evidence: Churn rise looks like price sensitivity (exit surveys, Inkwell) and like a cohort mix effect (promotion, activation)
2023 precedent says SMB increases pay off; Inkwell says conditions have changed
CFO's $10.3M vs renewal timing and contract caps

reasoning_traps.text: Treating blended churn as one number and concluding price sensitivity everywhere (or nowhere)
Reading exit surveys without splitting by cohort
Generalising the 2024 new-signup test to renewing customers without caveat
Accepting 'onboarding will halve SMB churn' without evidence, cost or timing

key_tradeoffs.text: ARR uplift vs churn risk, by segment
Competing with Inkwell in SMB (price) vs monetising mid-market/enterprise value
Short-term revenue vs NRR/brand (customer trust at renewal)

plausible_recommendations.text: Differentiated increase: raise mid-market (and enterprise within caps); hold or restructure SMB (grandfather, a lower-priced tier vs Inkwell, fix activation), with a staged test and churn guardrails.
Raise mid-market/enterprise now; delay SMB changes until the promotion cohort has washed out and activation is fixed.
A smaller uniform increase (e.g. 5–7%) with SMB grandfathering — defensible if the segment evidence is addressed.
No increase anywhere because 'churn is rising'.

defensibility_criteria: Separates the cohort/mix effect from a rate effect
Recognises both interpretations and reconciles them with the evidence
Pricing recommendation differs by segment or explains why it should not
